title: Cedar Bank - Data residency & compliance discovery
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-30 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Liam O'Connor, Maya Singh (Redwood); Rachel Monroe, Carlos Vega, Tom Nguyen, Asha Patel, Ben Keller (Cedar Bank)

Summary: quick discovery with Cedar Bank to understand data residency and compliance constraints for potential Redwood deployment. Focus on GDPR, financial services log retention, HIPAA adjacency, and whether Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fit their controls. Asked about audit logs, KMS, and restricted logging of PII. Agreed next steps: share SOC 2 / HIPAA / EU data residency docs, propose architecture diagrams for VPC Private deployment, schedule technical deep dive and pilot pricing.

[00:00] Liam: hey everyone, thanks for joining; uh we're recording this — quick intros, i'm liam on the account side and maya is our se, go ahead rachel?
[00:12] Rachel: yeah hi rachel monroe, head of data at cedar bank. we're evaluating LLM infra for internal assistant and customer-facing summaries. main question is where data lives and how logs are handled.
[00:25] Carlos: carlos vega, ciso — short on time but need to cover compliance: SOC2, GDPR, log retention, access controls.
[00:33] Tom: tom, platform, curious about networking — VPC, peering, private endpoints.
[00:40] Asha: asha, compliance — HIPAA overlap for some healthcare-adjacent clients, also financial regs, so strict PII rules.

[01:05] Liam: great — high level, redwood offers hosted, dedicated, and private options. hosted is fastest but data centres may be in multiple regions; dedicated gives you reserved capacity and isolation; private gives you a customer-controlled control plane (VPC or on-prem). maya, maybe you can walk through the compliance bits?
[01:20] Maya: sure. i'll try to be brief — we have SOC 2 Type II, we have (we're working on) HIPAA BAAs with select customers, and we can support EU-only residency for model inputs/outputs depending on deployment. for private deployments we can do customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit logs that integrate with your SIEM.
[01:45] Carlos: when you say "support EU-only residency" — does that mean we can guarantee that PII never leaves eu for processing? we have customers in germany who require that.
[01:58] Maya: short answer: yes for private and in many dedicated setups. for hosted, we can restrict region handling but need to check model availability per region. there are also fallback policies we need to discuss; we can lock routing to eu region endpoints, and with private we can guarantee all inference happens inside your VPC.
[02:20] Rachel: ok good. second, logs — when you run inference, what gets logged? we can't have prompts with account numbers or ssn logged in plaintext to any third-party system.
[02:33] Liam: totally, that's a common concern. by default we capture telemetry for performance purposes but we have configs: you can disable request/response logging, mask PII, and for private/dedicated customers we can configure no-persistence mode where user inputs aren't stored outside transient caches.
[02:50] Tom: does no-persistence still allow us to get token-level billing and latency metrics? we need usage cost breakdowns per product team.
[03:00] Maya: yes — you still get aggregate metrics and token counts, we can surface cost/latency per route without storing raw prompts. there may be tradeoffs in debugging fidelity.

[03:30] Carlos: read me the cryptographic controls — KMS integration? can you bring our AWS KMS or an on-prem HSM?
[03:40] Maya: we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM for private installations. for hosted we offer encryption-at-rest with our managed keys or customer-managed keys depending on contract. we can provide key rotation logs to your auditors.
[03:55] Asha: i need to know about audit logs retention — regulatory teams often require 7 years for some financial stuff. what retention windows are possible?
[04:08] Liam: retention is configurable; for hosted we have default retention windows, but enterprise agreements can extend retention and archive to your storage. for private, you control retention entirely.

[04:35] Rachel: we also have limits on what our teams can log due to PCI/PII — so SDKs need to let us redact or filter before sending. is that standard?
[04:45] Maya: yep our SDKs support client-side redaction hooks; many customers implement a pre-send middleware to strip card numbers and mask personal data. we also provide pre-built regex filters.

[05:15] Ben: what about model drift/regression monitoring — we need evals and regression alerts tied to our prompt sets.
[05:24] Maya: redwood optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts; that can be enabled with private/dedicated. hosted customers can also use it but we sometimes have to handle data residency for the evals.

[06:00] Rachel: timeline question — we want to decide by end of q1, start a pilot in q2. are there blockers you typically see?
[06:10] Liam: typical blockers are procurement/signing a DPA and BAA if HIPAA applies, and network connectivity for private deployments. procurement also requests SOC2 and encryption details — we'll send those.

[06:40] Tom: network — do you support private endpoints via AWS PrivateLink or customer VPC peering?
[06:48] Maya: both. we can do AWS PrivateLink, GCP VPC-SC patterns, or site-to-site VPN for on-prem. for dedicated we can also peering; it depends on latency requirements.

[07:10] Carlos: latency vs cost — our transactional flows need sub-200ms in some cases. how do we reconcile batching/caching with that?
[07:22] Maya: we have continuous batching and KV cache; you can tune batching windows and set latency SLOs. for sub-200ms you likely want dedicated GPUs in the region and small batch sizes, possibly model quantization to accelerate. we'll run benchmarks for your sequences.

[07:50] Rachel: can redwood guarantee model version pinning? we need reproducible outputs for audits.
[07:58] Liam: yes — you can pin exact model versions and we support rollouts/canary deployments so you can compare before switching.

[08:20] Asha: about HIPAA — you said you're working on BAAs; do you have customers in healthcare? any references?
[08:30] Maya: we have a couple of pilot customers under NDA; we can share a redacted BAA template and our security questionnaire responses. for full HIPAA production we typically recommend private or dedicated with a signed BAA.

[09:05] Ben: any limitations on logging obfuscation? e.g., do function calls / tools log arguments?
[09:12] Maya: tool calls can be configured to not persist, or to persist only sanitized metadata. we can also turn off function-arg logging per route.

[09:50] [interruption/static noise] Carlos: sorry, bit of lag here.
[10:10] Liam: no worries — quick question for tom: what's your expected traffic profile for the pilot? qps, average seq length?
[10:18] Tom: pilot is small — 5 qps peak, avg seq 150 tokens; production could be 50 qps during peak for certain products.
[10:30] Maya: good — for 150 token sequences we typically recommend a GPU with 48GB for cost-effective throughput, dedicated pools for consistent latency.

[11:00] Rachel: data residency nuance — some customers want EU-only residency but allow model weights to be managed elsewhere. is that acceptable?
[11:10] Maya: yes you can keep inference inputs/outputs in eu while model artifacts are hosted by us elsewhere, but some customers require the model and weights to be on-prem too. we can support both with private on-prem deployments.

[11:40] Carlos: encryption of logs in transit — do you support mutual TLS and client certs?
[11:48] Maya: mutual TLS is supported for private endpoints and dedicated; hosted uses TLS with certificate pinning and can support mTLS at partnership level.

[12:10] Liam: procurement often asks for a data flow diagram — we'll attach one. anything specific you want included?
[12:18] Asha: show where PII might surface, where logs land, retention, and who has access. must show audit log export to our SIEM.

[12:35] Maya: noted. we'll include key rotation, KMS boundaries, and a sample role-based access control matrix.

[13:05] Ben: competitors — we've been looking at BigCloudAI and OpenServe. what differentiates you on compliance?
[13:14] Liam: we emphasize production-first controls, private deployments that give customers full control over keys and logs, and a clear set of controls for dedicated pools. also our optimize tooling helps reduce cost while meeting latency/quality targets.

[13:40] Rachel: vendor risk management will want our legal team to see CISO-to-CISO answers. carlos will lead that. carlos: any specific asks?
[13:50] Carlos: send SOC2 report, penetration test summary, vulnerability management policy, and our standard security questionnaire answered.
[14:00] Maya: we'll send SOC2 Type II report, summary of pentest results, and a completed security questionnaire. we'll also include the BAA template.

[14:20] Rachel: sounds good. also, ping on whether you can do gradient-based explainability on sensitive fields — not blocking but nice to know.
[14:30] Maya: that is more on our research side; we can involve our applied ML folks in the technical deep dive if you want.

[15:00] Liam: next step idea: we'll share a docs bundle (SOC2, HIPAA BAA template, data residency whitepaper, network diagram) and propose a technical deep dive next week with maya + infra to discuss VPC/Private deployment. we'll also provide pricing for a 3-month pilot on dedicated capacity.

[15:30] Tom: one more Q — does private deployment require new hardware procurement or can you run inside our existing cluster?
[15:40] Maya: we have an on-prem appliance option but also can deploy into your kubernetes cluster if it meets GPU and networking reqs. we can send the hardware and k8s requirements.

[16:05] Rachel: what's the usual lead time for private?
[16:12] Liam: private on-prem can be 8-12 weeks typically; dedicated in our cloud region usually 2-4 weeks after contract; hosted is immediate.

[16:35] [background chatter] Ben: ROI/Unit cost question — do you have benchmark sheets that show tokens/sec and cost per 1M tokens by config?
[16:44] Maya: yes we'll share benchmark spreadsheet and a sample cost model tailored to your seq lengths.

[17:05] Asha: for audit readiness — do you provide exportable audit logs in a vendor-neutral format?
[17:12] Maya: yes — logs can be exported to S3, GCS, or pushed to your SIEM in JSON/CEF depending on your tooling.

[17:40] Rachel: okay recapping: we need security pack, BAA, data flow diagram, benchmark sheet, pilot pricing, and a technical deep dive scheduled.
[17:50] Liam: exactly — i'll own pricing and scheduling, maya will own technical diagram and benchmarks. carlos will coordinate vendor risk docs.

[18:15] Carlos: timeline for docs? before next tuesday ideally.
[18:22] Liam: we'll aim to send the initial bundle by 2027-01-04.

[18:40] Maya: quick note — for the pilot we'll recommend a dedicated pool in eu-west-1 to meet residency and latency. we'll include runbooks for token redaction.

[19:05] Tom: thanks everyone.
[42:10] [wrap up] Liam: thanks all for your time — notes and next steps in email. meeting ended.
summary: Discovery focused on Cedar Bank's data residency and compliance needs. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments, KMS/HSM support, logging controls and retention, network connectivity (PrivateLink/VPC), latency tradeoffs, HIPAA/BAA and SOC2 requirements. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send SOC2/BAA/security pack, architecture diagrams, benchmark sheet, and pilot pricing; schedule technical deep dive.
next_steps: Liam to send SOC2, HIPAA BAA template, data residency whitepaper, and network diagram by 2027-01-04.
Maya to prepare technical deep dive and benchmark spreadsheet; propose dedicated eu-west-1 pilot config.
Schedule technical deep dive with Cedar infra (Carlos/Tom) for week of 2027-01-10.
action_items: Liam O'Connor: send pricing and security docs (SOC2, BAA, pentest summary) by 2027-01-04.
Maya Singh: deliver benchmark spreadsheet, architecture diagram, and runbook for PII redaction by 2027-01-06.
Carlos Vega (Cedar): share vendor risk questionnaire and schedule infra meeting by 2027-01-07.
